To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Cd toxicity in maize plants is characterized by a dose-dependent decrease in growth parameters, chlorophyll content and enzyme activities.
the growth parameters of maize plants (cv. Volga) cultivated in a nutrient culture solution were not affected until the Cd concentration reached
Cd toxicity affects growth, mineral and pigment content, and activities of enzymes related to the cellular antioxidant system of young maize plants.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the biochemical effects induced by the presence of Cd in maize plants, and the establishment of a critical value for Cd content in plant tissues, which may be used as a reference for phytotoxicological studies.
the effects of Cd on the growth and development of young maize plants, and the possible use of some enzyme activities as early biomarkers of Cd stress.
the development of a sensitive and reliable bioassay based on enzyme activities, which can be used to assess the phyticotoxicity of Cd contaminated soils on maize plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of enzyme activities in the 3th and 4th leaves of maize plants as biomarkers of Cd toxicity is a promising approach for the assessment of Cd phytotoxicity in soils, but the use of the 4th leaves is preferable to that of the 3th leaves.
Cd uptake by maize plants is not lethal, but that the plant may be damaged by a reduction in growth and a modification of enzyme activities, especially in the leaves.
Cd is a toxic element to maize plants and that the critical value of Cd in plants for phytotoxicity is 3 mg Cd/kg dry matter in the third leaf and 5–10 mg Cd/kg dry in the fourth leaf.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cd toxicity effects on maize plants are related not only to the Cd content in the plant tissues but also to the activity of the antioxidant enzymes.
the use of the enzyme activities as a tool for early detection of Cd toxicity in plants is a promising approach.
the enzyme activities may be more sensitive indicators of Cd phytotoxicity in young maize plants than the growth parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of enzyme activities as biomarkers for Cd toxicity may be more sensitive than growth parameters.
the measurement of enzyme activity can be used as an early biomarker for Cd toxicity in maize plants.
the measurement of enzyme activity may be included as an early biomarker in a plant bio-assay to assess the toxicity of Cd-contaminants soils on maize.
